about: I am an independent software developer focused on building practical, reliable software systems for businesses and organizations. My work spans business management platforms, database infrastructure, desktop applications and intelligent automation.

I enjoy solving real operational problems by combining the right technologies into systems that are maintainable, secure and designed around the people who use them — approaching every project with a focus on understanding requirements, thoughtful architecture, quality implementation and long-term usability.

I am a student in Taiwan and I learn by building: the systems in this portfolio are real projects I have shipped end to end, independently, with AI as a co-pilot. I am still early in my journey, open to freelance work, and growing toward being a well-rounded full-stack and infrastructure developer.
Outside of code, I serve at my church, organising the Bible-verse display during services.

projects.name: JIL Church System
projects.tagline: Hybrid multi-tenant church platform, live in production
description: The flagship. A multi-tenant church management platform for the Jesus Is Lord church network, built on Google Apps Script and now backed by a hybrid database — Google Sheets and a self-hosted PostgreSQL store running side by side, kept in live sync.

It runs on a four-tier architecture — Master Dashboard, Regional, Church Template, and Church — so every congregation gets its own secure engine while the network sees across all of them. One codebase serves every church, routed by tenant.

People sign in once with their Google identity and see only the tabs their role allows, guarded server-side. Members register and check in by QR, attendance rolls up across regions, and it's engineered to scale toward thousands of churches.
highlights: Hybrid data backbone — Google Sheets ↔ self-hosted Postgres, kept in live sync
Four-tier design: Master Dashboard → Regional → Church Template → Church
Google-identity sign-in with many server-side permission guards
Role-filtered dashboards — sign in once, see only your role's tabs
QR registration and door check-in on any phone
Cross-church attendance across regions, analytics, automated email invites

caseStudy.problem: A growing church network tracked attendance and membership by hand, across scattered spreadsheets — no shared view across congregations, and data was easy to lose or duplicate.
caseStudy.solution: I built a multi-tenant platform on Google Apps Script with a four-tier design (Master Dashboard → Regional → Church Template → Church), Google-identity sign-in with server-side permission guards, QR registration and check-in, and a hybrid Google Sheets ↔ self-hosted PostgreSQL backbone kept in live sync.
caseStudy.results: One codebase now runs every church, with role-filtered dashboards, cross-church attendance roll-ups and automated invites — live in production and engineered to scale toward thousands of churches.

projects.name: JIL NEXUS
projects.tagline: The self-hosted database backbone — the hybrid half
description: NEXUS is the self-owned database I built to sit underneath the church system — a self-hosted Supabase (PostgreSQL) stack running in Docker on my own machine, designed to minimise recurring cloud costs (hardware, power and internet still apply).

The point is the hybrid: the live Google Sheets system and NEXUS run side by side for safety, data is copied across and verified by matching counts, and new registrations flow Sheets → NEXUS automatically over a Cloudflare tunnel. It's the backbone designed to carry the system toward an architectural target of ~1,000,000 records across thousands of churches — a design goal, not yet load-tested.
highlights: Self-hosted Supabase / PostgreSQL in Docker — designed to cut recurring cloud costs
Runs in parallel with Google Sheets for safety during migration
Live auto-sync: new registrations flow Sheets → Postgres over a Cloudflare tunnel
Count-matched migration across every church for data integrity
Architectural target: ~1,000,000 records across thousands of churches (design goal, not yet load-tested)

images.caption: Supabase Studio — the self-hosted JIL NEXUS database, live on my machine

projects.name: ARK | Business Hub
description: ARK is a complete business hub and point-of-sale for a pig farm, built as a Google Apps Script web app on a Google Sheets backend.

It runs the whole operation from one dashboard: tracking pigs and their weights, recording sales, logging expenses, and managing funds and investor contributions — with a monthly summary, an expense breakdown, an investment summary, and a full audit log of who changed what and when. Access is split across farm managers and investors by role.
highlights: Dashboard, Pigs, Funds, Expenses, Sales, Team and Audit-Log tabs
Pig inventory with weight tracking and sales recording (POS)
Expense breakdown and monthly summaries
Investor contributions and investment summary
Role-based access for managers and investors
Audit log — who changed what and when

images.alt: ARK Business Hub dashboard showing pig-farm funds, expenses, sales and monthly summary
images.caption: ARK dashboard — funds, expenses, sales & monthly summary (demo data)

caseStudy.problem: A pig farm ran sales, expenses, livestock and investor funds across notebooks and loose spreadsheets — with no clear view of profit, and no record of who changed what.
caseStudy.solution: I built a complete POS and management hub on Google Apps Script and Google Sheets — pig inventory with weight tracking, sales, expense breakdowns, investor contributions, monthly summaries and a full audit log, all split by role.
caseStudy.results: The whole operation now runs from one dashboard, with clear monthly summaries and a full audit trail — managers and investors each see exactly what they need.

projects.name: Church Presentation Studio
projects.tagline: Desktop app that hears Scripture and shows it live
description: A cross-platform desktop presentation app for church services, built with Tauri 2, React/TypeScript and a Rust core over SQLite.

It imports and edits PowerPoint, renders native Scripture slides, and — the standout — detects Bible references from the pastor's microphone in real time and puts the verse on screen, with dual-screen HDMI output. It's designed to plug into the JIL Church System as an added feature of the same hybrid ecosystem.
highlights: Real-time Bible-reference detection from the pastor's microphone
Native Scripture slides plus PowerPoint import/edit
Dual-screen HDMI output for live services
Rust + SQLite core; cross-platform (Windows & macOS)
Built to connect into the JIL Church System
